subject: Demo recap: decision flow, procurement checklist & action owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Rivers <ellen.rivers@staterahealth.com>, Mark DuVall <mark.duvall@staterahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap: decision flow, procurement checklist & action owners

Hi Ellen / Mark —

Thanks again for your time today. Nice walkthrough — appreciate the candid notes about latency targets and the internal review steps. Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed next steps and who owns what so we don’t lose momentum. Below is a compact recap + three asks for the week:

Quick recap (from our demo):
- Goal: Replace current edge deployment for clinical summarization with hosted + private deployment for PHI workloads (pilot: 2 models, 10k daily inference tokens).
- Key SLOs: 99.9% availability during business hours, p95 latency < 450ms for 512-token responses.
- Decision criteria highlighted: latency, audit logs/KMS support, cost per 1M tokens, and contract language around data residency.

Stakeholder map (as discussed) — please confirm or correct:
- Economic buyer: Mark DuVall (CFO) — responsible for TCO and contract sign-off.
- Security/Compliance reviewer: Amir Qureshi (Head of InfoSec) — will validate SOC2, KMS, and audit logs.
- Procurement/Legal: Ellen Rivers — primary procurement contact.
- Technical lead: Dr. Priya Natarajan (ML Platform) — will run the pilot and validate perf.

Action owners & timeline (proposed):
1) Redwood: share a short procurement checklist + baseline SLO language (Jordan / Marissa) — by Thu 9/9. [Attachment: Procurement-Checklist.xlsx]
2) Redwood: price banding for pilot vs. projected steady-state + optional Dedicated pricing (Ben) — by Fri 9/10.
3) Statera: confirm economic buyer email and procurement PO process; share any non-negotiable T&Cs to surface early (Ellen) — by Fri 9/10.
4) Joint: schedule a 30-min procurement review between legal/procurement + Redwood legal (target week of 9/13).

Three asks for this thread (easy wins):
- Ellen / Mark: confirm the economic buyer and the procurement contact to loop in (if different from Ellen).
- Amir (or security delegate): confirm the SOC2 artifacts they require or a point person — we can prepare a short evidence deck.
- Statera: flag any specific contract terms that will require early negotiation (e.g., data residency, indemnity caps).

Attachments: RWDW-Demo-Slides.pdf (demo deck), Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (short checklist + sample MSA clauses).

I’ll follow up with the checklist and a lightweight MRP (mutual readiness plan) draft. If this layout looks right, I’ll create a HubSpot plan and tentative meeting times for the week of 9/13.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Attachment(s): RWDW-Demo-Slides.pdf
From: Ellen Rivers <ellen.rivers@staterahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark DuVall <mark.duvall@staterahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Demo recap: decision flow, procurement checklist & action owners

Jordan —

Thanks for the tight recap. This is very helpful. Confirmations and notes below:

- Economic buyer: yes, Mark DuVall (mark.duvall@staterahealth.com). He’ll want a 3-year TCO projection but will prioritize pilot cost visibility first.
- Security contact: Amir Qureshi (amir.qureshi@staterahealth.com) — he asked for SOC2 Type II report, KMS key management diagram, and an outline of audit-log retention. I’ll try to get a calendar invite for an intro call if you can send the evidence deck.
- Procurement: that’s me for now; procurement may loop in a purchasing manager later for PO specifics. Our standard procurement exceptions: data residency clause (we host PHI in us-east only), and a liability cap tied to contract value. I’ll flag anything else once legal reviews your checklist.

A few immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you send a short sample MSA excerpt showing data residency and KMS/keys language we can share with legal?
2) Estimated monthly cost for the pilot (approx tokens/day x 30) and a high-level cost range for a Dedicated pool if pilot scales to 5k QPS over peak (ballpark is fine).

We’ll aim to get Amir and our legal lead on the procurement review next week. I also attached the internal vendor onboarding questionnaire we run — Ben, Marissa: you might find the answers helpful.

Best,
Ellen
Procurement Lead, Statera Health
ellen.rivers@staterahealth.com
Attachment(s): Statera-Vendor-Questionnaire.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Rivers <ellen.rivers@staterahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap: decision flow, procurement checklist & action owners

Ellen — thanks for the confirmations. I’m attaching the procurement checklist and a short MSA excerpt that addresses data residency and KMS controls. High-level notes here so legal has context before the call:

What we attached:
- Procurement-Checklist.xlsx — table with required artifacts, owners, and estimated delivery dates (SOC2, KMS diagram, audit log export formats).
- MSA-Excerpt.txt — sample clauses: data residency (customer can request region pin), KMS & key-escrow language, and retention windows.

Ben — can you draft two price scenarios by EOD Friday:
A) Pilot pricing (1 model, 10k daily tokens) — usable hosted + private routing cost
B) Scale estimate (Dedicated pool) — 3-year committed rate + monthly cadence.

Jordan — I’ll create the HubSpot mutual action plan and propose slots for a 30-min legal/procurement sync next Tue/Wed (9/14 or 9/15). I’ll also prepare the evidence deck for Amir with SOC2 highlights and a KMS diagram.

Ellen — two quick Qs that will help prep the deck:
- Do you need the full SOC2 report or is a summary + key control screenshots enough for Amir initially?
- Any regulatory constraints beyond HIPAA we should be aware of?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
